name: semver
description: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: parse, compare, sort and bump versions, and match Cargo and npm version ranges

api.name: Ident
api.sig: pub type Ident = NumId{n: Int} | StrId{s: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One pre-release identifier: a number (compared numerically) or an alphanumeric word
(compared in ASCII order). Numbers sort before words.

api.name: Version
api.sig: pub type Version = {major: Int where _ >= 0, minor: Int where _ >= 0, patch: Int where _ >= 0, prerelease: List[Ident], build: List[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A version `major.minor.patch[-prerelease][+build]`. Build metadata never affects precedence.

api.name: VersionErr
api.sig: pub type VersionErr = EmptyVersion | WrongPartCount{found: Int} | BadNumber{part: Str} | LeadingZero{part: Str} | NumberTooLarge{part: Str} | EmptyIdentifier{section: Str} | BadIdentifier{ident: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Why a text is not a valid version. `part` is the offending piece of the input.

api.name: Part
api.sig: pub type Part = Major | Minor | Patch | Prerelease | Build derive Eq, Show
api.doc: The highest component in which two versions differ.

api.name: Op
api.sig: pub type Op = OpEq | OpGt | OpGe | OpLt | OpLe derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A comparison operator of a range comparator.

api.name: Comparator
api.sig: pub type Comparator = {op: Op, ver: Version} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One comparator, such as `>=1.2.0`.

api.name: Range
api.sig: pub type Range = {sets: List[List[Comparator]]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A range: a version matches when it matches every comparator of at least one set. An empty
set matches every version (pre-releases only with include_prerelease).

api.name: RangeErr
api.sig: pub type RangeErr = {text: Str, reason: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Why a text is not a valid range: `text` is the offending comparator or the whole input.

api.name: version
api.sig: fn version(major: Int where _ >= 0, minor: Int where _ >= 0, patch: Int where _ >= 0) -> Version
api.doc: The release version `major.minor.patch`, with no pre-release or build.

api.name: parse
api.sig: fn parse(s: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc:
Parses a version exactly as SemVer 2.0.0 writes it: three numbers without leading zeros,
then optional `-` pre-release and `+` build identifiers. No surrounding spaces or `v`.

api.name: parse_loose
api.sig: fn parse_loose(s: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc:
Parses like `parse` after trimming spaces and dropping any leading `=`, `v` or `V`
characters (`" =v1.2.3 "` is 1.2.3). Everything after them must still be a strict version.

api.name: is_valid
api.sig: fn is_valid(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: True when `s` is a strict SemVer 2.0.0 version.

api.name: coerce
api.sig: fn coerce(s: Str) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc:
The first version-like run of digits in `s`, as node-semver's `coerce`: up to three
dot-separated numbers, missing ones are 0, and anything around them (a `v`, a fourth number,
a pre-release) is ignored: `"v1.2"` is 1.2.0, `"1.2.3.4"` is 1.2.3, `"x 7 y"` is 7.0.0.
A number too large for `Int` makes the result `none`.

api.name: describe_error
api.sig: fn describe_error(e: VersionErr) -> Str
api.doc: A readable message for a version error.

api.name: format_version
api.sig: fn format_version(v: Version) -> Str
api.doc: The canonical text of a version, `1.2.3-rc.1+build.5`.

api.name: compare
api.sig: fn compare(a: Version, b: Version) -> Int
api.doc:
SemVer precedence (spec item 11): -1, 0 or 1. Numbers compare numerically, a pre-release
is lower than its release, identifiers compare left to right, and build metadata is ignored.

api.name: compare_total
api.sig: fn compare_total(a: Version, b: Version) -> Int
api.doc:
A total order consistent with `==`: precedence first, then build metadata (none first,
then identifier by identifier, numeric ones numerically and before alphanumeric ones, as the
Cargo `semver` crate orders them).

api.name: impl Ord for Version
api.sig: impl Ord for Version
api.doc: `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` on versions follow `compare_total`.

api.name: precedence_eq
api.sig: fn precedence_eq(a: Version, b: Version) -> Bool
api.doc: True when the two versions have the same precedence (they may differ in build metadata).

api.name: sort_versions
api.sig: fn sort_versions(vs: List[Version]) -> List[Version]
api.doc:
The versions in ascending `compare_total` order (stable). The builtin `sort` is structural
and does not follow SemVer order, so use this instead.

api.name: sort_versions_desc
api.sig: fn sort_versions_desc(vs: List[Version]) -> List[Version]
api.doc: The versions in descending `compare_total` order.

api.name: highest
api.sig: fn highest(vs: List[Version]) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc: The highest version by `compare_total`, `none` for an empty list.

api.name: lowest
api.sig: fn lowest(vs: List[Version]) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc: The lowest version by `compare_total`, `none` for an empty list.

api.name: diff
api.sig: fn diff(a: Version, b: Version) -> Opt[Part]
api.doc: The highest component in which `a` and `b` differ, `none` when they are equal.

api.name: is_prerelease
api.sig: fn is_prerelease(v: Version) -> Bool
api.doc: True when `v` has pre-release identifiers.

api.name: is_stable
api.sig: fn is_stable(v: Version) -> Bool
api.doc: True when `v` is a release with major version 1 or more: SemVer's stable public API.

api.name: is_compatible
api.sig: fn is_compatible(base: Version, candidate: Version) -> Bool
api.doc:
True when `candidate` can replace `base` under Cargo's default (caret) rule: the same
leftmost non-zero component and not lower; pre-releases only of the same `major.minor.patch`.

api.name: release
api.sig: fn release(v: Version) -> Version
api.doc: The release without pre-release or build identifiers.

api.name: strip_build
api.sig: fn strip_build(v: Version) -> Version
api.doc: `v` without build metadata.

api.name: with_prerelease
api.sig: fn with_prerelease(v: Version, text: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc: `v` with the pre-release identifiers parsed from `text` (`"rc.1"`); `""` removes them.

api.name: with_build
api.sig: fn with_build(v: Version, text: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc: `v` with the build identifiers parsed from `text` (`"sha.5114f85"`); `""` removes them.

api.name: bump_major
api.sig: fn bump_major(v: Version) -> Version
api.doc:
The next major version, as npm's `inc`: 1.2.3 becomes 2.0.0, and a pre-release of a major
version (2.0.0-rc.1) becomes that release. Build metadata is dropped.

api.name: bump_minor
api.sig: fn bump_minor(v: Version) -> Version
api.doc: The next minor version: 1.2.3 becomes 1.3.0, and 1.3.0-rc.1 becomes 1.3.0.

api.name: bump_patch
api.sig: fn bump_patch(v: Version) -> Version
api.doc: The next patch version: 1.2.3 becomes 1.2.4, and 1.2.4-rc.1 becomes 1.2.4.

api.name: bump_pre
api.sig: fn bump_pre(v: Version, id: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc:
The next pre-release, as npm's `inc("prerelease", id)`: a release gets the next patch and
`-id.0` (1.2.3 to 1.2.4-rc.0); a pre-release whose first identifier is `id` (or any when `id`
is "") gets its last number incremented (1.2.4-rc.0 to 1.2.4-rc.1) or `.0` appended; another
identifier restarts at `-id.0`. `id` must be "" or an alphanumeric identifier that is not a
number; otherwise the result is an error.

api.name: bump_premajor
api.sig: fn bump_premajor(v: Version, id: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc: The next major version as a first pre-release: 1.2.3 with "rc" becomes 2.0.0-rc.0.

api.name: bump_preminor
api.sig: fn bump_preminor(v: Version, id: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc: The next minor version as a first pre-release: 1.2.3 with "rc" becomes 1.3.0-rc.0.

api.name: bump_prepatch
api.sig: fn bump_prepatch(v: Version, id: Str) -> Res[Version, VersionErr]
api.doc: The next patch version as a first pre-release: 1.2.3 with "rc" becomes 1.2.4-rc.0.

api.name: any_range
api.sig: fn any_range() -> Range
api.doc: The range that matches every release (`*`).

api.name: exact
api.sig: fn exact(v: Version) -> Range
api.doc: The range `=v`: only versions with the same precedence as `v`.

api.name: caret
api.sig: fn caret(v: Version) -> Range
api.doc:
The caret range `^v`: from `v` up to the next change of its leftmost non-zero component
(^1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <2.0.0-0, ^0.2.3 is >=0.2.3 <0.3.0-0, ^0.0.3 is >=0.0.3 <0.0.4-0).

api.name: tilde
api.sig: fn tilde(v: Version) -> Range
api.doc: The tilde range `~v`: from `v` up to the next minor version (~1.2.3 is >=1.2.3 <1.3.0-0).

api.name: range_or
api.sig: fn range_or(a: Range, b: Range) -> Range
api.doc: A version matches `range_or(a, b)` when it matches `a` or `b`.

api.name: range_and
api.sig: fn range_and(a: Range, b: Range) -> Range
api.doc: A version matches `range_and(a, b)` when it matches both `a` and `b`.

api.name: parse_cargo
api.sig: fn parse_cargo(s: Str) -> Res[Range, RangeErr]
api.doc:
Parses a Cargo version requirement: comparators separated by commas, each `^`, `~`, `=`,
`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` or none (a bare version is a caret requirement, a bare wildcard such as
`1.2.*` an exact one), with partial versions and `*`, `x` or `X` wildcards. Spaces around operators are allowed.
Cargo has no `||`, hyphen ranges or `v` prefixes, so those are errors, as is an empty text.

api.name: parse_npm
api.sig: fn parse_npm(s: Str) -> Res[Range, RangeErr]
api.doc:
Parses an npm (node-semver) range: sets separated by `||`, each a space-separated list of
comparators (`>=1.2.7 <1.3.0`) or one hyphen range (`1.2 - 2.3.4`). Comparators take `=`,
`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `~` (or `~>`), `^` or no operator, partial versions, `x`, `X` and `*`
wildcards, and a `v` or `=` before the version. A bare version is exact, a partial one an
X-range (`1.2` is >=1.2.0 <1.3.0-0), and an empty set means any version. Derived upper bounds
are written `<2.0.0-0`, as node-semver does, so pre-releases of the bound never match.

api.name: parse_npm_with
api.sig: fn parse_npm_with(s: Str, include_prerelease: Bool) -> Res[Range, RangeErr]
api.doc:
Like `parse_npm` with node-semver's `includePrerelease` reading: lower bounds that come from
partial versions and wildcards are written with `-0` (`1.x` is >=1.0.0-0 <2.0.0-0), so with
`matches_with(r, v, true)` the pre-releases inside the range match too.

api.name: matches
api.sig: fn matches(r: Range, v: Version) -> Bool
api.doc:
True when `v` matches `r`. A pre-release matches only a set with a comparator of the same
`major.minor.patch` that has a pre-release itself (so `>=1.2.3-beta` takes 1.2.3-rc but not
1.2.4-rc), the rule both Cargo and npm follow.

api.name: matches_with
api.sig: fn matches_with(r: Range, v: Version, include_prerelease: Bool) -> Bool
api.doc:
Like `matches`, but `include_prerelease` drops the pre-release rule, as node-semver's
option of that name: a pre-release then matches whenever every comparator holds.

api.name: filter_matching
api.sig: fn filter_matching(vs: List[Version], r: Range) -> List[Version]
api.doc: The versions of `vs` that match `r`, in their order.

api.name: max_satisfying
api.sig: fn max_satisfying(vs: List[Version], r: Range) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc: The highest version of `vs` that matches `r`.

api.name: min_satisfying
api.sig: fn min_satisfying(vs: List[Version], r: Range) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc: The lowest version of `vs` that matches `r`.

api.name: intersects
api.sig: fn intersects(a: Range, b: Range) -> Bool
api.doc:
True when some version, counting pre-releases (the `include_prerelease` reading), matches
both `a` and `b`. Exact: it knows that nothing lies between 1.0.0 and 1.0.1-0.

api.name: min_version
api.sig: fn min_version(r: Range) -> Opt[Version]
api.doc:
The lowest version that can match `r` under `include_prerelease`, as node-semver's
`minVersion`: 0.0.0 or 0.0.0-0 when they match, else the lowest of the sets' tightest lower
bounds (`>1.2.3` gives 1.2.4, `>1.2.3-rc` gives 1.2.3-rc.0) when it matches; `none` when no
such version matches.

api.name: format_range
api.sig: fn format_range(r: Range) -> Str
api.doc:
The canonical text of a range, in node-semver's form: comparators joined by spaces, sets by
` || `, an empty set as `*` (`parse_npm("^1.2")` gives `>=1.2.0 <2.0.0-0`).
